mainTopic: Gifts by document: the שכיב מרע's "write and give," and the wording "מהיום ולאחר מיתה" for a father's gift to his son
overview: The amud opens by finishing an earlier case: a שכיב מרע who said "write and give." His request for a document only adds strength to the gift, like רב חסדא's קנין, so the הלכה is that we write and we give. Then a new משנה begins. רבי יהודה says a father giving his property to his sons must write "from today and after death," while רבי יוסי says this is not needed. The משנה adds that in such a gift neither the father nor the son can sell alone: the father's sale lasts only until his death, and a buyer from the son must wait until the father dies. The גמרא explains that in a gift, unlike a גט, these words mean the property itself is given today and the produce after death. A story with רבה בר אבוה shows that the הלכה follows רבי יוסי, because the date on the שטר already shows when the gift starts. The אמוראים then discuss whether a written act of transfer makes the wording unnecessary, and whether the order of the phrases matters. The final version says it does not. The amud ends by setting up a new case, a son who sold the property and died before his father, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The document only adds strength, like רב חסדא's קנין
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains why we carry out the instruction of a שכיב מרע who said "write and give." His request for a document was meant only to strengthen the gift, just as in רב חסדא's case where a קנין was added to a gift.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is like what רב חסדא said about a will that reads "and we made a קנין from him in addition to this gift." Here too, the man said: "Also write and sign a document, and give it to him."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues its explanation from the previous page. It shows that the sick man's words "write and give" do not make the gift depend on a document.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry was that the sick man wanted the gift to work only through a document, and a document cannot transfer anything once he has died. The גמרא answers that the word "also" shows the document was meant as an extra boost on top of the gift. This matches רב חסדא's ruling, where a קנין added to a gift is only meant to strengthen it.

keyTerms.meaning: A seriously ill person whose spoken instructions can transfer property
"And we made a קנין (formal act of acquiring) from him"
Here too: applies the same idea to the current case
Write, sign, and give it to him

phrases.english: As Rav Chisda said:
"And we made a kinyan from him
in addition to this gift";
here too, where he said:
"Also write and sign and give it to him."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the explanation of שמואל's view from the previous page
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterprets the sick man's words as adding strength (ייפוי כח), not as a condition
steps.terutzHavaAmina: He wanted the gift to work only through a document, which cannot work after death
steps.terutzMaskana: The document is an extra; the gift itself stands, so we write and give

steps.title: The הלכה: we write and we give
steps.stepSummary: Two chains of אמוראים rule that the הלכה is: we write the document and give the gift.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל that the הלכה is that we write and we give. רבא also said in the name of רב נחמן that the הלכה is that we write and we give.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final practical ruling on the case of the sick man who said "write and give."
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two separate teachers, רב יהודה quoting שמואל and רבא quoting רב נחמן, give the same ruling. This settles the matter: we follow the view that the gift stands, so the document is written and the money is given.

keyTerms.meaning: It was stated: introduces a teaching of the אמוראים
We write the document and we give the gift

steps.whatToRemember: When a שכיב מרע says "write and give," the הלכה is that we write and we give. The document only adds strength to his gift.

phrases.english: It was stated: Rav Yehuda said in the name of Shmuel,
the halacha is: we write and we give.

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן אָמַר רָבָא אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן,
phrases.english: And so said Rava in the name of Rav Nachman,
the halacha is: we write and we give.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל הֲלָכָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the practical ruling that follows from the explanation in step 1
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה is כותבין ונותנין: we write the document and give the gift.

steps.title: משנה: must a father write "from today and after death"?
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה. רבי יהודה says a father who writes his property to his sons must write "from today and after death." רבי יוסי says he does not need to.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: One who writes his property to his sons must write "from today and after death." These are the words of רבי יהודה. רבי יוסי says: he does not need to.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with a מחלוקת about the wording a father needs when he gives his property to his sons.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A healthy father wants his sons to get the property while he keeps using it until he dies. רבי יהודה requires the exact words "from today and after death" for this to work. רבי יוסי says this wording is not needed.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה (written in the text as מַתְנִי׳)
From today and after death: the son owns the property now, but the father keeps using it until he dies

phrases.english: Mishnah:
One who writes his property to his sons,
must write
"from today and after death,"
these are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.
Rabbi Yosei says: he does not need to.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic in a new משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה requires the wording "מהיום ולאחר מיתה"; רבי יוסי says it is not required.

steps.title: Neither father nor son can sell the property
steps.stepSummary: When a father writes his property to his son to take effect after his death, the father cannot sell it because it is written to the son, and the son cannot sell it because it is still in the father's possession.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who writes his property to his son for after his death: the father cannot sell it, because it is written to the son. The son cannot sell it, because it is in the father's possession.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues and explains the result of such a transfer: each side holds only part of the rights.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ownership is split. The son already owns the property on paper, so the father cannot sell it away. The father still holds it and uses it during his lifetime, so the son cannot sell it either.

keyTerms.meaning: In the father's possession or control

steps.whatToRemember: With this kind of transfer, the son holds ownership on paper and the father holds the use during his life, so neither one can sell alone.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not read "after his death" as meaning the son gets nothing until then. The son already has ownership that blocks the father from selling. The father keeps only the use of the property while he lives.

phrases.english: One who writes his property to his son for after his death:
phrases.notes: This case works like "from today and after death." The son owns the property now, and the father keeps using it.

phrases.english: the father cannot sell,
because they are written to the son;
and the son cannot sell,
because they are in the possession of the father.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַכּוֹתֵב נְכָסָיו לִבְנוֹ לְאַחַר מוֹתוֹ הָאָב אֵינוֹ יָכוֹל לִמְכּוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה by explaining the rights that result from the transfer
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Neither the father nor the son can sell: the property is written to the son but remains in the father's possession.

steps.title: What happens when the father or the son sells the property
steps.stepSummary: The משנה finishes its ruling. A sale by the father lasts only until he dies. A buyer from the son gets nothing until the father dies.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the father sold the property, it is sold only until he dies. If the son sold it, the buyer has no rights in it until the father dies.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes the case from the previous step. It explains what happens when either the father or the son goes ahead and sells.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The son owns the property itself, but the father keeps the use and produce while he is alive. So a buyer from the father gets only the produce for the father's lifetime. A buyer from the son must wait until the father dies, and then he gets the property.
steps.confusionAlert: Step 4 said neither one can sell, but here a sale does work in part. The father's sale covers only the produce during his life, and the son's sale covers only the property after the father dies.

phrases.english: If the father sold, they are sold until he dies.

phrases.aramaic: מָכַר הַבֵּן – אֵין לַלּוֹקֵחַ בָּהֶן כְּלוּם
phrases.english: If the son sold, the buyer has nothing in them
until the father dies.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the משנה's ruling from step 4 by saying what happens if a sale actually takes place.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A father's sale lasts only until his death. A son's sale takes effect only after the father's death.

steps.title: How can "from today and after death" work, when it makes a גט doubtful?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי יהודה's wording helps at all. A משנה about גיטין says that the same words make a גט only doubtful.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he writes "from today and after death," what does that accomplish? We learned that a גט given "from today and after death" is a doubtful גט. If the husband dies, she does חליצה but not יבום.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יהודה's wording from step 3. It points out that these exact words leave a גט in doubt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the case of the גט, nobody knows whether the husband meant "today" or "after death," so the divorce is uncertain. Since she might still be married to him, she needs חליצה. Since she might be divorced, she may not do יבום. If the words are unclear for a גט, how can they be clear enough for a gift?

keyTerms.meaning: a divorce document that is not fully a divorce document; a doubtful גט

phrases.english: GEMARA

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי כָּתַב ״מֵהַיּוֹם וּלְאַחַר מִיתָה״, מַאי הָוֵי?
phrases.english: And if he wrote "from today and after death," what of it?
But we learned:
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in גיטין 72a.

phrases.english: "From today and after death" — it is a גט and not a גט;
and if he dies, she does חליצה but does not do יבום!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי כָּתַב מֵהַיּוֹם וּלְאַחַר מִיתָה מַאי הָוֵי הָא תְּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא by questioning the wording רבי יהודה required in the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's requirement to write "from today and after death"
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same wording leaves a גט in doubt, so it should not be able to create a clear gift.

steps.title: A gift is different: the property is given today, the produce after death
steps.stepSummary: With a גט, it is unclear whether "after death" is a condition or a retraction. With a gift, it clearly means the property is given today and the produce after death.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, we are unsure whether "after death" is a condition or a retraction. But here, this is what he is telling him: acquire the property itself from today, and the produce after death.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The גט case and the gift case are different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a גט, we cannot tell whether "after death" is a condition on "from today" or a retraction of it, so the divorce is doubtful. With a gift, the two phrases do not clash, because they refer to different things. The son owns the property itself now, and he gets the produce when the father dies. This also explains the rules about selling in step 5.

keyTerms.meaning: a retraction, taking back what was said

steps.whatToRemember: "From today and after death" in a gift means the property itself belongs to the son today, while the produce stays with the father until he dies.
steps.whyThisMatters: This split between the property and its produce is the reason the father can sell only the produce for his lifetime, and the son can sell only the property itself.

phrases.english: There, we are unsure
phrases.notes: "There" means the case of the גט.

phrases.aramaic: אִי תְּנָאָה הָוֵי, אִי חֲזָרָה הָוֵי;
phrases.english: whether it is a condition, or whether it is a retraction;
but here, this is what he is saying to him:
acquire the property itself from today,
the produce after death.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם מְסַפְּקָא לַן אִי תְּנָאָה הָוֵי אִי חֲזָרָה הָוֵי אֲבָל הָכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases: a גט versus a gift
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The wording is just as unclear in a gift as it is in a גט.
steps.terutzMaskana: In a gift, the words split ownership: the property itself is given today, and the produce after death.

steps.title: רב הונא wants to ask the sick רבה בר אבוה whether the הלכה follows רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי יוסי's view. While visiting the sick רבה בר אבוה, רב הונא tells רב נחמן to ask him whether the הלכה follows רבי יוסי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: he does not need to write it. רבה בר אבוה was sick, and רב הונא and רב נחמן went in to visit him. רב הונא said to רב נחמן: ask him whether the הלכה follows רבי יוסי or not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to רבי יוסי's opinion in the משנה and tells a story. It is setting up a question about the practical הלכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי holds that the father does not need to write "from today and after death." The question is whether we rule like him in practice. רב הונא wants רב נחמן to ask this of their sick colleague.

phrases.english: רבי יוסי says: he does not need to.
phrases.notes: These are the words of the משנה from step 3: he does not need to write "from today and after death."

phrases.english: רבה בר אבוה became sick,

phrases.aramaic: עָל לְגַבֵּיהּ רַב הוּנָא וְרַב נַחְמָן.
phrases.english: רב הונא and רב נחמן went in to him.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לֵיהּ רַב הוּנָא לְרַב נַחְמָן, בְּעִי מִינֵּיהּ:
phrases.english: רב הונא said to רב נחמן: ask him:
is the הלכה like רבי יוסי,
or is the הלכה not like רבי יוסי?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from רבי יהודה's wording to the second view in the משנה, רבי יוסי's.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the practical הלכה follows רבי יוסי, so that the father does not need to write "from today and after death."

steps.title: רב נחמן hesitates: how can I ask about the הלכה without knowing the reason?
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן objects that he does not understand רבי יוסי's reasoning. He asks how he can ask about the הלכה before knowing it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I do not know רבי יוסי's reasoning. Should I ask him about the הלכה?
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן pushes back on רב הונא's request. He does not feel ready to ask the question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן feels that asking for a ruling makes little sense before he understands the reason behind רבי יוסי's view. He would first want to know why רבי יוסי holds that the extra wording is not needed.

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: רב נחמן is speaking to רב הונא.

phrases.english: I do not know רבי יוסי's reasoning,
should I ask him about the הלכה?

steps.triggerLanguage: טַעְמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי לָא יָדַעְנָא הֲלָכָה אֶיבְעֵי מִינֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רב נחמן objects to רב הונא's request in step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's request to ask about the הלכה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It makes little sense to ask for a ruling before understanding the reasoning behind it.

steps.title: רב הונא: you ask about the הלכה, and I will tell you the reason
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא tells רב נחמן to go ahead and ask about the הלכה. He promises to explain רבי יוסי's reasoning himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: you ask him whether the הלכה follows him or not, and I will tell you his reasoning.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא answers רב נחמן's hesitation. This sets up the next part, where רבי יוסי's reasoning will be explained.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא removes the problem by dividing the work between them. רב נחמן asks for the ruling, and רב הונא supplies the reason. Now the question can go ahead.

keyTerms.meaning: whether it is the הלכה or not

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: Now רב הונא is answering רב נחמן.

phrases.aramaic: אַתְּ בְּעִי מִינֵּיהּ אִי הֲלָכָה אִי לָא,
phrases.english: You ask him whether it is the הלכה or not,
and his reasoning I will tell you.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַתְּ בְּעִי מִינֵּיהּ אִי הֲלָכָה אִי לָא וְטַעְמֵיהּ אֲנָא אָמֵינָא לָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב נחמן's objection in step 9 and sets up the explanation of רבי יוסי's reasoning.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical answer: dividing the task between the two of them
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב נחמן cannot ask about the הלכה because he does not know the reasoning.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב נחמן should ask, and רב הונא will supply the reasoning.

steps.title: The הלכה Follows רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן asks, and רבה בר אבוה answers in the name of רב that the הלכה follows רבי יוסי.
steps.simpleTranslation: He asked him. He answered: this is what רב said, the הלכה follows רבי יוסי.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן follows רב הונא's advice and asks the sick רבה בר אבוה his question. He gets a clear ruling: the הלכה follows רבי יוסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This finishes the visit story from step 8. The answer comes as a tradition from רב, not as reasoning of his own. That is why רב הונא still has to explain the reason afterward, as he promised in step 10.

phrases.english: He asked him.
phrases.notes: רב נחמן is asking רבה בר אבוה, the sick man they were visiting.

phrases.english: He said to him: this is what Rav said:
The halacha follows Rabbi Yosei.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ. אֲמַר לֵיהּ, הָכִי אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Carries out the plan from step 10: ask about the הלכה first.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the הלכה follow רבי יוסי?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes. רב said the הלכה follows רבי יוסי.

steps.title: רב הונא Explains רבי יוסי's Reason
steps.stepSummary: After they leave, רב הונא explains that for רבי יוסי the date on the document proves when it takes effect.
steps.simpleTranslation: After they left, רב הונא said to רב נחמן: this is רבי יוסי's reason. He holds that the date of the document proves it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא keeps his promise from step 10 and explains why רבי יוסי says the words 'from today' are not needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The date written on the שטר already shows that the gift starts on that day. So the document does not need to say 'from today' outright. The words 'after death' can only refer to the produce, which the father keeps until he dies.

keyTerms.meaning: The date written on the document
Proves about it, shows what it means

phrases.english: After they left,
he said to him:
phrases.notes: רב הונא is speaking to רב נחמן.

phrases.english: This is the reason of Rabbi Yosei,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר: זְמַנּוֹ שֶׁל שְׁטָר מוֹכִיחַ עָלָיו.
phrases.english: for he says: the date of the document proves about it.
phrases.notes: The date shows the gift starts that day, so there is no need to write 'from today.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the reasoning that רב נחמן said he was missing in step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The date of the שטר shows that the gift starts that day.

steps.title: A ברייתא Confirms the Reason
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי יוסי giving exactly this reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught this way: רבי יוסי says he does not need to write it, because the date of the document proves it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that supports רב הונא's explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא's reason is not his own guess. The ברייתא shows that רבי יוסי himself gave this reason, word for word.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught this way, in a ברייתא

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי יוסי, the date on a שטר already shows when the gift starts, so 'from today' does not need to be written.

phrases.english: It was also taught this way:
Rabbi Yosei says: he does not need to,
phrases.notes: He means he does not need to write 'from today and after death.'

phrases.aramaic: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁזְּמַנּוֹ שֶׁל שְׁטָר מוֹכִיחַ עָלָיו.
phrases.english: because the date of the document proves about it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 12 with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: רב הונא's explanation of רבי יוסי
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא in which רבי יוסי gives the same reason

steps.title: רבא Asks About a Gift Made With a קנין
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks רב נחמן what the law is when an act of transfer was done.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא asked רב נחמן: when there was a הקנאה, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question begins. רבא asks whether a הקנאה removes the need to write 'from today and after death.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the question was about the wording alone. Now רבא asks whether a formal act of transfer settles the matter by itself.

keyTerms.meaning: An act of transfer, a קנין

phrases.english: Rava asked Rav Nachman:
With an act of transfer, what is the law?
phrases.notes: He means a gift made with a קנין. Does he still need to write 'from today'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new related question about gifts made with a קנין.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does a הקנאה make 'from today and after death' unnecessary?

steps.title: With a קנין, It Is Not Needed
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן answers that with a הקנאה there is no need to write it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: with a הקנאה, he does not need to write it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן answers רבא: when a קנין was done, the extra wording is not needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The act of transfer itself shows that the gift starts now. So it does the same job as the words 'from today.'

phrases.english: He said to him:
With an act of transfer, he does not need to.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's question from step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: With a הקנאה, 'from today and after death' is not needed.

steps.title: רב פפי: It Depends on the Order of the Wording
steps.stepSummary: רב פפי says some transfers still need the wording and some do not. It depends on which phrase comes first in the document.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפי said: some transfers need it and some do not. If the document says 'He transferred to him and we acquired from him,' it is not needed. If it says 'We acquired from him and he transferred to him,' it is needed.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפי qualifies רב נחמן's answer. Not every הקנאה works; the order of the words in the document matters.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן gave one rule for every הקנאה. רב פפי splits it into two cases. When 'he transferred' comes first, the extra wording is not needed. When 'we acquired' comes first, it still is. The גמרא does not explain here why the order matters.

keyTerms.meaning: We, the witnesses, acquired from him

steps.confusionAlert: רב פפי is not disagreeing that a קנין can help. He is saying that it helps only when the document is worded in the right order.

phrases.english: Rav Pappi said:
There is a transfer where he needs to,
and there is a transfer where he does not need to.
"He transferred to him, and we acquired from him":
phrases.notes: These are words the witnesses write in the document. 'We' means the witnesses.

phrases.english: he does not need to.
"We acquired from him, and he transferred to him":
he needs to.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב פַּפֵּי אָמַר: אִיכָּא אַקְנְיָתָא דִּצְרִיךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows רב נחמן's general rule into two cases.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Whether a הקנאה makes the wording unnecessary depends on whether 'he transferred' or 'we acquired' comes first in the document.

steps.title: רב חנינא: Would Only the Scribes Know This?
steps.stepSummary: רב חנינא מסורא objects that the חכמים do not know such a distinction, so it is strange to think the scribes would.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חנינא מסורא objected: is there anything that we, the חכמים, do not know, but the scribes do?
steps.whatsHappening: רב חנינא challenges רב פפי's distinction. It is so fine a point that even the חכמים do not know it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפי's distinction depends on how scribes word a document, yet the חכמים themselves had never heard of it. רב חנינא asks whether there could really be a rule the חכמים do not know but the scribes do. His point is that the distinction is probably not a real one.

phrases.english: Rav Chanina of Sura objected to it:

phrases.aramaic: מִי אִיכָּא מִידֵּי דַּאֲנַן לָא יָדְעִינַן,
phrases.english: Is there anything that we do not know,
and the scribes know?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב פפי's distinction in step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפי's rule that the order of the wording matters
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A distinction the חכמים do not know is unlikely to be real law known only to scribes.

steps.title: The Scribes Did Know the Distinction
steps.stepSummary: They asked the scribes of אביי and of רבא, and both groups knew the distinction.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked the scribes of אביי, and they knew. They asked the scribes of רבא, and they knew too.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רב חנינא's objection by checking with real scribes. Both groups of scribes knew the distinction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חנינא assumed scribes could not know such a detail. Experience shows that experienced scribes did know it, so the objection falls away and רב פפי's distinction holds.
steps.whatToRemember: רב פפי's distinction about the order of the words survives רב חנינא's objection, because the scribes of אביי and רבא knew it. Steps 19 and 20 bring a different view, that the order does not matter at all.

phrases.english: They asked the scribes of Abaye, and they knew,
and the scribes of Rava, and they knew.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 17 by showing that the scribes really knew the distinction.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Factual check that disproves the objection's assumption
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Scribes could not know a distinction the חכמים do not know.
steps.terutzMaskana: The scribes of אביי and רבא knew it, so רב פפי's distinction stands.

steps.title: Order of the phrases does not matter
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע rules that whenever a transfer is mentioned, in either order, 'from today' is not needed. The מחלוקת is only about a document that just records what happened.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא son of רב יהושע said: Whether the document says 'he transferred to him and we acquired from him,' or 'we acquired from him and he transferred to him,' there is no need to write 'from today.' They argue only about a document that says 'a record of what happened before us.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע disagrees with רב פפי's distinction. He says the order of the phrases makes no difference at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפי said it depends on which phrase comes first. רב הונא says that any mention of a transfer is enough, so no extra wording is needed. That leaves the מחלוקת of רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי only for a document that never mentions a transfer, just 'what happened before us.'

keyTerms.meaning: We acquired it from him (the witnesses did the act of acquisition)
A record of the proceedings, a plain report of what happened

phrases.aramaic: רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אָמַר:
phrases.english: Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua said:
Whether "he transferred to him and we acquired from him,"
or "we acquired from him and he transferred to him" —
it is not needed;
phrases.notes: What is not needed is the extra phrase from the משנה, 'from today and after my death.'

phrases.english: and they disagree about "a record of the proceedings that took place before us."
phrases.notes: 'They' means רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי from the משנה.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different view from רב פפי's distinction, which the previous steps had defended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Any mention of a transfer, in either order, makes 'from today' unnecessary. The מחלוקת is only about a plain record.

steps.title: Another version of רב נחמן's teaching
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא reports that רב זביד of נהרדעא learned רב נחמן's teaching differently: as one flat statement that matches רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said: I told this teaching to רב זביד of נהרדעא, and he said to me: You learn it this way, but we learn it this way. רבא said in the name of רב נחמן: Where there is a transfer, the extra wording is not needed. Whether it says 'he transferred to him and we acquired from him' or 'we acquired from him and he transferred to him,' it is not needed. They argue only about 'a record of what happened before us.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב זביד tells רב כהנא that in נהרדעא they learned רב נחמן's teaching as one rule, not as a question and answer. In that version, the order of the phrases makes no difference.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the version from earlier steps, רבא asked a question, רב נחמן answered, and רב פפי added a distinction. In רב זביד's version, רב נחמן himself says plainly that the order does not matter. So רב נחמן's own words already say what רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע said.

keyTerms.meaning: You teach it / we teach it (the way a teaching is passed on)

steps.whatToRemember: In the final version, any written act of transfer, in either order, is enough without 'from today.' רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי argue only about a document that just records what happened.
steps.confusionAlert: רב זביד is not adding a new opinion. He is giving a different version of how רב נחמן's words were passed down.

phrases.english: Rav Kahana said:
I said this teaching
before Rav Zevid of Neharde'a,
and he said to me:
You teach it this way;
phrases.notes: He means the way it was taught earlier: רבא's question, רב נחמן's answer, then רב פפי's distinction.

phrases.english: we teach it this way:
Rava said that Rav Nachman said,
where there is a transfer, it is not needed —
whether "he transferred to him and we acquired from him,"
or "we acquired from him and he transferred to him" — it is not needed.
They disagree about "a record of the proceedings that took place before us."

steps.triggerLanguage: אַתּוּן הָכִי מַתְנִיתוּ לַהּ אֲנַן הָכִי מַתְנֵינַן לָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע's view by showing that רב נחמן's teaching, as learned in נהרדעא, says the same thing.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב נחמן: with any written transfer, in either order, 'from today' is not needed. The מחלוקת is only about a plain record.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The order of the phrases does not matter. Only a plain 'record of proceedings' is under dispute.

steps.title: Back to the משנה: property written to a son for after death
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about a father who writes his property to his son for after his death, to open a new discussion.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who writes his property to his son for after his death.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the words of the משנה to start a new topic. This is a setup line that points us to the case about to be discussed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the discussion was about how the document is worded. Now the focus moves to what each person may do with the property. The father still uses it during his life, but the son will own it after the father dies.

keyTerms.meaning: One who writes (grants in a document) his property

phrases.english: One who writes his property to his son for after his death.
phrases.notes: This is a quote from the משנה in step 4, where neither the father nor the son can sell the property on his own.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the wording discussion and opens a new section based on the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Quotes the משנה's case of a father who gives his property to his son for after his death.

steps.title: The case: the son sold, then died before the father
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא presents a case: the son sold the property while his father was alive, and then the son died before the father.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: The son sold the property during the father's lifetime, and the son died during the father's lifetime —
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is laying out a case of a son who sold the property and then died before his father. This is setup; the question about this case and the opinions on it come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says that if the son sells, the buyer gets nothing until the father dies. Here the son died first, so he never lived to own the property fully. The coming discussion asks whether the buyer gets anything when the father later dies.

keyTerms.meaning: It was stated (introduces a teaching or dispute of the אמוראים)

phrases.english: It was stated: The son sold during the father's lifetime,
and the son died during the father's lifetime —

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds a specific new case on the משנה just quoted.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets up the case: the son sold and died during the father's lifetime. The ruling follows.
